message.content:
Yes, the original Coca-Cola formula did contain cocaine, though in trace amounts from coca leaf extract.

Here's the history:

- **Original formula (1886)**: When pharmacist John Pemberton invented Coca-Cola in Atlanta, Georgia, he included coca leaf extract as one of the key ingredients. At the time, cocaine was legal and commonly used in patent medicines and tonics. The drink's name "Coca-Cola" actually derives from two of its original ingredients: the **coca** leaf (source of cocaine) and the **kola** nut (source of caffeine).

- **Cocaine removal**: The active cocaine was removed from the formula in **1903** (some sources say 1901 or 1904). The company switched to using "spent" or de-cocainized coca leaves, which maintained the flavor profile without the drug. This change was driven by shifting public attitudes toward cocaine, increasing regulation, and changing social perceptions of the drug.

- **Today**: Coca-Cola still uses coca leaves for flavoring, but they are specially processed to remove all cocaine. The de-cocainized leaves are supplied to Coca-Cola under strict DEA supervision, while the extracted cocaine is used for medical and research purposes.

The original formula also contained kola nut extract (for caffeine), sugar, phosphoric acid, caramel coloring, and various natural flavorings including vanilla, lime, and other essential oils.

Sources:
1. https://oboe.com/learn/the-secret-coca-cola-formula-cf0ias/evolution-of-the-formula-the-secret-coca-cola-formula-1
2. https://vocal.media/fyi/the-history-of-cocaine-from-coca-cola-to-toothaches
3. https://www.thetakeout.com/1788713/why-coca-cola-had-cocaine/
4. https://thetraininggyms.com/blog/coca-cola-is-worse-than-cocaine/
5. https://coca-cola.fandom.com/wiki/The_Coca-Cola_formula
